concerns.text: User Story 1 (Core Spatial Memory Implementation) lacks explicit anchoring for the 'interference distance' metric defined in US-3. While US-1 mentions 'comparing recall accuracy', it does not explicitly anchor the specific 'interference distance' measurement (FR-011) to this story, creating a gap where the primary validation metric for the spatial hypothesis is not clearly tied to the core implementation story.

FR-010 mandates capping the dataset to '[deferred] of the original size'. This placeholder is not anchored to any User Story or resolved in the spec text. The plan.md resolves this to '10%', but the spec itself must contain the concrete value or an explicit reference to the plan's resolution to be testable. Currently, it is an unbacked requirement.

FR-011 requires computing 'interference distance' but the spec does not define the mechanism for 'adjacent grid coordinates' or how 'unrelated items' are determined. This ambiguity makes the requirement untestable as written. The requirement text must explicitly define the injection protocol (e.g., 'inject semantically unrelated items into adjacent coordinates defined by...') to be anchored to a testable story.

The Assumptions section contains a fragmented sentence with unresolved placeholders: '[Citation]', '[Research Question]', and '[Method]'. This text is not anchored to any User Story and leaves the basis for the interference distance threshold and batch size reduction logic undefined. This violates the requirement for a clear, testable specification.

FR-003 states the system 'MUST reduce batch size... if peak memory usage exceeds 6 GB RAM'. The spec does not define the 'peak memory usage' measurement point (e.g., per batch, per epoch, or total process RSS) or the threshold for 'exceeds 6 GB' (e.g., >6.0 GB or >=6.0 GB). This ambiguity makes the requirement untestable and unanchored to a specific implementation logic.

FR-005 requires 'paired two-tailed t-tests' but does not specify the null hypothesis (e.g., 'mean difference = 0'). While 'two-tailed' implies a non-directional test, the explicit statement of the hypothesis is missing, making the requirement untestable as the implementer cannot determine the exact statistical test to run.

FR-006 requires 'family-wise error correction... when >1 hypothesis test is run'. The spec does not define the set of tests to which this correction applies (e.g., 'across the 3 datasets' or 'across all seeds and datasets'). This ambiguity affects the implementation and makes the requirement unanchored to a specific statistical protocol.

FR-007 requires computing 'Cohen's d effect size with 95% confidence intervals' but does not specify the formula (e.g., pooled standard deviation vs. standard deviation of the difference) or the method for calculating the confidence interval. This lack of specificity makes the requirement untestable.

FR-008 requires computing and logging 'slot occupancy distribution for every epoch' but does not define the format of this distribution (e.g., histogram bins, list of counts per slot). Without a defined output format, the requirement is ambiguous and unanchored to a specific data structure.

FR-009 requires computing and logging 'coordinate variance for every epoch' but does not specify whether this is the variance of the x-coordinates, y-coordinates, or the combined 2D variance. This ambiguity makes the requirement untestable.

SC-006 states 'the spatial variant is considered successful if it demonstrates a statistically significant reduction in interference' but does not define the threshold for 'statistically significant' in this context (e.g., p < 0.05 after correction). While SC-004 mentions α = 0.05, SC-006 does not explicitly reference it, creating a potential disconnect.

The Edge Cases section states: 'If memory usage still exceeds 6 GB at batch size 4, total samples are capped at [deferred] of the original.' This repeats the '[deferred]' placeholder found in FR-010. The spec must resolve this to a concrete value (e.g., '10%') or explicitly reference the plan's resolution to ensure the edge case handling is fully specified and testable.
